chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir and Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The pilgrim is in one of three states: a man who performed Hajj al-Ifrad with the offering of a sacrificial animal, a man who performed Hajj al-Ifrad without taking the offering, and a man who performed Hajj al-Tamattu by combining Umrah with Hajj.

key_terms.إِفْرَاد: Ifrad (a type of Hajj where one performs only Hajj)
key_terms.تَمَتُّع: Tamattu (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.سِيَاقُ الْهَدْيِ: Siyag al-Hady (bringing the sacrificial animal along)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Hajj in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* delineates the three canonical modes of Hajj—Ifrad, Qiran, and Tamattu—emphasizing the ritual requirement of the Hady (sacrificial animal) as the primary differentiator between Ifrad and Qiran. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is crucial for determining the specific rites and exemptions applicable to the pilgrim, reflecting the Prophet’s practice as interpreted by the Imams. The hadith underscores the structural integrity of the pilgrimage rites, linking ritual form directly to spiritual obligation.
